Surah al-Humazah (The Slanderer)

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿Woe﴾ is a mubtada' (subject of a nominal sentence), and its khabar (predicate) is: ﴿to every backbiter and mocker﴾, that is, the one who disparages people behind their backs.

﴿Mocker﴾: that is, one who disparages them to their faces. The pattern fu'alah (in ﴿humazah﴾ and ﴿lumazah﴾) indicates that this is a habit of his. It has been said: it was revealed concerning al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, whose habit was backbiting and defaming. It has also been said: concerning Ubayy ibn Khalaf, and it has been said: concerning al-Walid. It is permissible that the cause of revelation be specific while the warning is general, so that it encompasses everyone who engages in that vile conduct.

﴿Alladhī﴾ is a *badal* (substitute, or apposition) for "kull," or it is in the accusative on the basis of censure (*naṣb ʿalā al-dhamm*).

﴿jamaʿa māl-an﴾. "*Jammaʿa*" is read by al-Shāmī, Ḥamzah and ʿAlī. It is an intensive form (*mubālagha*) of "*jamaʿa*," and it agrees with His saying: ﴿wa-ʿaddadahu﴾, meaning He made it a reserve (*ʿuddah*) against the calamities of time.

He thinks that his wealth has made him immortal (akhladahu). That is, it has left him living forever in this world, never dying. Or it is an allusion (ta'ridh) to righteous deeds: it is they that make their doer abide in bliss, whereas wealth has never made anyone abide in anything.

(p-679) ﴿Nay!﴾ — a rebuke to him for his reckoning (that his wealth would make him immortal).

﴿He will surely be thrown﴾ — i.e., the one who gathered [wealth],

﴿into the Huṭamah﴾ — into the Fire, which is of such a nature that it breaks to pieces everything cast into it.
﴿And what will make you know what the Crushing Fire is?﴾ This is an expression of wonder and of magnification...

Note on the request: the passage is a short grammatical comment on the verse, and I'll translate it as it stands.

﴿Nārullāh﴾ (the Fire of Allah) is the predicate (khabar) of an omitted subject (mubtada'), i.e., "it is the Fire of Allah,"

﴿al-Mūqadah﴾ (the kindled one) is its attribute (na't).

Surah 104, verse 7: "Which mounts over the hearts."

The commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil):

﴿Which mounts over the hearts﴾. That is, it penetrates into their insides until it reaches their chests and mounts over their af'idah (hearts), which are the midst of the hearts. Nothing in the human body is more subtle than the fu'ad (heart), and nothing is more prone to pain from the slightest harm that touches it. So how much more so when the Fire of Jahannam mounts over it and overpowers it.

It was said: He specified the af'idah because they are the seats of disbelief and corrupt beliefs. The meaning of the Fire's mounting over them is that it encompasses them.

﴿Indeed, it will be closed over them﴾. That is: the Fire, or: al-Hutamah (the Crusher),

﴿closed﴾, meaning: sealed shut.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 104, verse 9:

"Fī ʿumudin" (with two dammas), read by Kūfī (ʿĀṣim's reading) except Ḥafṣ; the rest read "fī ʿamadin." Both are two dialectal forms of the plural of ʿimād (pillar), like ihāb and uhub, and ḥimār and ḥumur.

﴿In extended columns﴾: meaning, the doors are shut upon them, and the columns are extended over the doors, for making (them) doubly secure, in securing (them).

In the hadith: "The believer is shrewd and perceptive, and cautious and steadfast; he does not hasten, he is learned and scrupulous. The hypocrite is a backbiter and slanderer, a glutton, like the firewood-gatherer of the night, who does not care from where he acquires (wealth) or on what he spends it."
